c-m2-circle.label: Circle: area, circumference and what scales
c-m2-circle.summary: Area grows as the square of the radius, circumference as the radius. Compare shapes before computing.

c-m2-ring.label: Rings and pathways (annulus)
c-m2-ring.summary: A ring is the outer circle minus the inner: π(R² − r²) = π(R − r)(R + r).

c-m2-sector.label: Sectors, arcs and central angles
c-m2-sector.summary: A sector is a fraction θ/360° of a circle; arc = rθ when θ is in radians.

q-m2-part.short: Part or ratio of a circle
q-m2-part.label: Part of a circle, or area ratio of similar circles
q-m2-part.summary: A fraction of a garden is cultivated; the ratio of areas of two circles; the part of a circumference in a turn.

q-m2-compare.label: Same wire: circle against square
q-m2-compare.summary: The same perimeter makes a circle or a square; compare the areas.

q-m2-ring.label: Area of a ring or a path around a circle
q-m2-ring.summary: Outer and inner radius given; area of the ring, or its ratio to the whole.

q-m2-sector.label: Sector angle, arc length and area
q-m2-sector.summary: Arc and radius give the angle; two sectors of one circle are compared.

formulas.text: Area = πr²     Circumference = 2πr     with π = 22/7 when the radius is a multiple of 7
Similar figures: area ratio = (ratio of lengths)²
Same perimeter P: circle area = P²/(4π), square area = P²/16
Ring = π(R² − r²) = π(R − r)(R + r)     Ring ÷ whole circle = (R² − r²) ÷ R²
formulas.note: Pathway of width w around radius r: R = r + w.

formulas.text: Sector area = (θ/360°) × πr²     Arc = rθ (θ in radians)     180° = π rad

q-m2-part.cue: 'A garden, 80% cultivated…', 'two similar circles with radii in the ratio…', 'percentage of circumference in a half turn'.
q-m2-part.standard: Find the whole (πr²) and take the fraction asked: 20% of 22/7 × 28 × 28 = 492.8 cm². For ratios use the radius ratio squared.
q-m2-part.fast: 22/7 × 28 × 28 = 22 × 4 × 28 = 2,464; 20% of it = 492.8. For a half turn the answer is 50% whatever the radius.
q-m2-part.eliminate: Ask what is being asked: 'uncultivated' is the small part (20%), so the answer is a fifth of the area, and the radius cancels in a half-turn question.
traps: Taking the cultivated 80% instead of the remaining 20%.
Giving the radius ratio (5 : 8) instead of the area ratio.
Spending time on the radius when only the fraction matters.

q-m2-compare.cue: 'The same length of wire is used for a circle or a square. Ratio of the areas?'
q-m2-compare.standard: Perimeter 80 m: square side 20, area 400. Circle: 2πr = 80, r = 40/π, area = πr² = 1,600/π ≈ 509.3. Ratio ≈ 1.27 : 1.
q-m2-compare.fast: The ratio is 4/π whatever the wire length: 4 ÷ 3.14 = 1.27.
q-m2-compare.eliminate: A circle always holds more area than a square with the same perimeter, so the ratio is above 1 (removes 1 : 1). And 4/π is a little over 1.27.
traps: Assuming equal perimeter means equal area.
Using the diameter as the radius.

q-m2-ring.cue: A circular garden with a pathway of width w around it; an annular region with outer and inner radii.
q-m2-ring.standard: Ring = π(R² − r²). Path around r = 18 with w = 2.5: R = 20.5, area = 22/7 × (20.5² − 18²) = 22/7 × 96.25 = 302.5 m². Ratio of ring to outer circle for R = 12, r = 8: (144 − 64)/144 = 5/9.
q-m2-ring.eliminate: The strip is about width × circumference at the middle: 2.5 × 2π × 19.25 ≈ 302. A strip of 2.5 around 18 is a bit more than 2.5 × 2π × 18 = 282.7.
traps: Using R = r + 2w when the path is only on the outside once.
Giving the radius ratio 8 : 12 = 2 : 3 as the area ratio.

q-m2-sector.cue: 'Central angle of a sector with arc … and radius …' or two sectors with angles in different units.
q-m2-sector.standard: Angle in radians = arc ÷ radius = 12 ÷ 4 = 3. For sectors of one circle compare angles in the same unit: 5π/6 rad = 150°, so the ratio is 1 : 1.
q-m2-sector.fast: Put both angles in degrees first. 5π/6 × 180/π = 150.
q-m2-sector.eliminate: Convert units before comparing: if the two angles look different (150° and 5π/6) they may be equal.
traps: Forgetting that the answer in radians has no units.

pyqs.text: A car wheel has a radius of 42 cm. What percentage of its circumference is covered in a half turn? (Use π = 22/7.)
solution: A half turn is half the circumference, whatever the radius.
pyqs.trick: The radius is a distractor; a half turn covers half the circumference.

pyqs.text: What is the central angle (in radians) of a sector with an arc length of 12 cm in a circle of radius 4 cm?
solution: Arc = r × θ, so θ = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 radians.
pyqs.trick: Angle in radians is just arc ÷ radius.

pyqs.text: A circular garden has a radius of 18 m. A 2.5 m wide pathway is built around it. What is the approximate area of the pathway?
pyqs.trick: The path is about width × the middle circumference: 2.5 × 2π × 19.25 ≈ 302.

pyqs.trick: For equal perimeters the ratio is always 4/π ≈ 1.27.

pyqs.text: A sector of a circle has a central angle of 150° and radius 10 cm. Another sector of the same circle has a central angle of 5π/6 radians. What is the ratio of the area of the first sector to that of the second?
solution: Both sectors have the same angle and radius, so the areas are equal: 1 : 1.
pyqs.trick: Convert 5π/6 into degrees before anything else.
